description: Search the web, news, images, scholarly papers, companies and people in one call. 2 credits per 10 results from each ...

categories.description: pdf: web results that are PDF files. research: scholarly papers, in a research list, ranked by relevance then citations. companies: companies that match the query, in a companies list, best matches first. The query can name a place, industry, employee count, founding year and funding stage, like fintech startups in Berlin, 50-200 employees. people: people that match the query, in a people list, best matches first. The query can name a role, company, place or research topic, like CFO of Stripe, founders of fintech startups in Berlin, or researchers on CRISPR base editing. Each person has roles, affiliations and public profile links, never contact details. developer: passages from GitHub READMEs, issues, merged pull requests, releases, developer docs and API operations, in a developer list; send it as an object to filter by repos, types, language and minStars.

language.description: Only repositories whose main language is this, like TypeScript.

minStars.description: Only repositories with at least this many GitHub stars.

repos.description: Only results from these GitHub repositories, as owner/name.

types.description: Only these result types: readme, issue, pull_request, release, operation, doc.

country.description: Two-letter country to search from, like us. Image results are always US.

highlights.description: On by default. When a web result's page is already stored, its description is the passages of that page that best match the query. Send false for the snippet the search engine shows.

ignoreInvalidURLs.description: Leave out results whose address cannot be read as a page.

limit.description: Most results to return for each source. Default 10, or 5 with scrapeOptions, which reads at most 5 pages. News returns at most 50.

location.description: Where to search from, like Germany or San Francisco,California,United States. The last part is the country and replaces country. A city before it narrows web results to that place.

maxAge.description: Accept a stored answer up to this many milliseconds old, at most 30 days. Without it, 15 minutes for news and 1 hour for web and images. 0 always searches live.

safe.description: Hide explicit web and image results when true.

scrapeOptions.description: Reads the top web results, up to 5, and puts the passages that best match the query in each description. Add formats to get more from each page: markdown, html, links, summary or {"type":"json","prompt":"the price"}. Costs 1 more credit for each page read, plus 4 for each summary or json with a schema or prompt that returns something.

options.description: Only with parser: extra inputs for it, such as { "page": 2 } for the next page of results or { "minRating": 4.5 } for a filter. GET /v1/parsers lists what each parser accepts.

parser.description: Read the page with a named parser, which gives the site's own data as json. The url must be the kind of page the parser reads. Parsers are the only way to read some sites. GET /v1/parsers lists them.

prompt.description: What to pull from the page in plain words, such as the version and the release date.

rules.description: Read the page with CSS rules instead of a model, no extra fee. Each field is a selector such as "h1" (the first match's text), "a@href" (an attribute) or { "selector": "li", "type": "list", "output": "text" | "html" | "@attribute" | { nested fields } }. A missing item is null and an unmatched list is []. Relative links become absolute. Up to 100 fields, 5 levels deep. Not with schema, prompt or parser.

schema.description: The fields to fill, as a JSON Schema (draft-07 or 2020-12) object with properties. Pydantic's model_json_schema() and zod's toJSONSchema() output work as they are. enum, const, anyOf, oneOf, nullable types, $ref with $defs, required, descriptions and any key names are read. Up to 100 top-level fields and 32 KB. A field the page does not state comes back null.

zeroDataRetention.description: Send true to keep nothing from the pages read, and read each one live. Costs 1 more credit per page.

sources.description: What to search: web, news, images. Each is a string or {type}. Default web, or none when categories asks for research, companies, people or developer.

tbs.description: Time filter: qdr:h, qdr:d, qdr:w, qdr:m or qdr:y, or cdr:1,cd_min:MM/DD/YYYY,cd_max:MM/DD/YYYY. Web takes both; news takes qdr only; images take none.

timeout.description: Milliseconds to wait for the sources.

name: stophy_search
title: Search
